A1.goal: Understand a few simple facts and recognise the speaker’s feelings.

gist.title: What does the man do at the start of his speech?
options: He tells everyone to sit down.
He thanks several people.
He sings a short song.
gist.why: He begins by thanking people on stage.

gist.title: How does the speaker sound for most of the speech?
options: Angry and impatient
Afraid and confused
Happy and thankful
gist.why: His voice is warm and grateful.

detail.title: How many things does he say he needs each day?
options: Two
Three
Four

detail.title: What does he say about his children?
options: He wants them to be proud of him.
He wants them to make films.
He wants them to come up on stage with him.
detail.why: He tells his children that he wants to make them proud.

detail.title: Which period of his life does he describe near the end?
options: His first day at university
A recent trip with his family
His life as a teenager
detail.why: The last part includes a story about his teenage years.

sequence: He talks about the other actors.
He talks about his family.
He tells a story about his hero.

facts.title: How many children does he name?
facts.hint: Write a number or a word.

open.title: Write one sentence: What does he say about one person in his family?
open.answer: He says his mother is here tonight. / He wants his wife and children to be proud of him.
open.criteria: One comprehensible sentence with a correct detail about a family member.

A2.goal: Follow the main message, identify key people and understand a few exact details.

gist.title: What is the speaker mainly doing?
options: Explaining how to enter the film business
Thanking people and sharing personal ideas
Describing the story of his latest film in detail
gist.why: He thanks people and gives a personal reflection.

gist.title: Which statement best describes the ending?
options: He apologises and leaves quickly.
He announces a new film project with his family.
He finishes in a positive, energetic way.
gist.why: The closing words are upbeat and warmly received.

detail.title: Who does he thank for directing the film?
options: Martin Scorsese
Christopher Nolan
Jean-Marc Vallée
detail.why: He names the director Jean-Marc Vallée.

detail.title: What does his mother teach him and his brothers?
options: To win every competition
To respect themselves
To travel around the world
detail.why: He says his mother taught them self-respect.

detail.title: What is his reaction when he is asked the question again ten years later?
options: He says the question no longer matters.
He says he has finally achieved it.
He says he has not achieved it yet.
detail.why: He answers that he is still far from the goal.

sequence: He talks about people from his film.
He talks about his father.
He speaks about his wife and children.

facts.title: How many older brothers does he mention?

open.title: Choose one person he talks about. What does he say about him or her?
open.answer: He thanks people who worked with him or talks warmly about family members.
open.criteria: Accept one relevant person/group and one clear example of appreciation.

B1.goal: Follow a personal narrative, recognise supporting details and explain a central idea.

gist.title: Which description best summarises the speech?
options: A report on the film industry and how it is changing
A personal thank-you that also gives a life lesson
A defence of why one film deserved to win
gist.why: He combines appreciation with a personal idea about life.

gist.title: Who does the speaker mainly address?
options: Mainly the other actors in his category who did not win
Mainly the director and the producers of the film
The people at the ceremony and a wider audience
gist.why: He speaks to the room and then broadens his closing message.

detail.title: How does he describe the other nominees’ performances?
options: He praises their acting.
He says they were disappointing.
He refuses to compare them.
detail.why: He compliments the other nominated performances.

detail.title: Who turns out to be the person he is trying to become?
options: A future version of himself
A famous actor he admired at school
An older relative who inspired his work
detail.why: He uses an imagined future self as an ideal.

detail.title: What happens in the last part of the speech?
options: He tells a final joke about his co-stars and the director
He tells the audience about the next film he will make
He returns to earlier ideas and closes energetically
detail.why: His conclusion echoes the speech’s earlier structure.

sequence: He recognises other people in the film business.
He says he needs three things every day.
He talks about his father.
He explains a lesson he learnt at home.

facts.title: Name ONE of the two co-stars he thanks near the beginning.

open.title: Choose a family memory from the speech and explain what it shows about his relationships.
open.answer: For example, he recalls a lesson from his mother and connects it with respect for other people.
open.criteria: Identify a real detail from the recording and explain its significance.

B2.goal: Identify detail and argument, trace the structure and interpret tone and purpose.

gist.title: Which headline best fits the whole speech?
options: A prize-winner explains why acting is an unusually difficult job.
Personal recognition becomes an opportunity for wider reflection.
An actor looks back on the decisions that built his career.
gist.why: He moves beyond the award and shares a broader personal perspective.

gist.title: Which best describes the overall progression?
options: From a list of films to a debate about which of them deserves the prize
From an argument with critics to an apology for his career
From acknowledgements to personal examples and a closing reflection
gist.why: The speech develops from thanks to a personal closing message.

detail.title: Why does he praise the other nominees early in the speech?
options: He recognises their work before focusing on himself.
He suggests the judges may have chosen the wrong winner.
He wants the other nominees to join him on stage.
detail.why: He acknowledges the quality of the other nominees’ work.

detail.title: How does his mother’s lesson develop?
options: Respect for oneself helps to build respect for others.
Respect is presented as something that must be earned through fame.
People should rely on their families rather than their own judgement.
detail.why: He describes self-respect as a foundation for respecting others.

detail.title: What is the effect of returning to a series of short phrases at the end?
options: It introduces an unexpected argument about politics and the industry.
It creates a memorable conclusion with a sense of completion.
It corrects what the speaker said earlier in the speech.
detail.why: The ending echoes earlier themes and creates closure.

sequence: He mentions the other nominees and his colleagues.
He names three things he needs every day.
He talks about his father.
He talks about his mother.

facts.title: Write the surname of the director he thanks.

open.title: Choose one moment in the speech and explain how it affects the audience.
open.answer: The speech moves between reverent appreciation and comic family images, making a formal moment feel personal.
open.criteria: Identify two contrasting tones and link the shift to a specific moment.

C1.goal: Analyse rhetorical choices, implied values and the speaker’s construction of a public persona.

gist.title: Which account best explains the speech’s broader purpose?
options: He argues that professional recognition is ultimately unimportant.
He uses a public honour to reflect on values and motivation.
He presents his success as the outcome of a carefully planned career.
gist.why: He uses a personal occasion to express wider guiding values.

gist.title: How is the speaker’s public persona chiefly established?
options: By offering an objective analysis of the competing performances
By challenging the audience’s understanding of cinema as an art
By combining professional status with intimate disclosure
gist.why: The speech joins a formal setting to personal storytelling.

detail.title: What is the effect of acknowledging his fellow nominees?
options: He frames his win within a respected group of performers.
He undermines the authority of the award before accepting it.
He implies the other nominees did not have enough experience.
detail.why: He positions himself appreciatively in relation to fellow artists.

detail.title: What is the causal link in the lesson attributed to his mother?
options: A strong sense of self-respect allows more respect for others.
Public success creates the confidence needed to respect others.
It is easier to gain respect by avoiding close relationships.
detail.why: He links respect for oneself with respect for other people.

detail.title: What is the main effect of the final series of short declarations?
options: They reconnect his themes with an informal public identity.
They reverse his earlier argument in favour of a new one.
They signal his disappointment with how the whole ceremony has gone.
detail.why: The memorable close returns to his themes in an informal voice.

sequence: He credits professional peers and collaborators.
He offers a general organising principle.
He turns to his late father.
He recalls a lesson from his upbringing.

facts.title: Give the surname of the director he thanks before naming the co-stars.

open.title: Choose two moments that sound very different and discuss the effect of the contrast.
open.answer: The formal acknowledgements establish professionalism; informal scenes and anecdotes make the speaker relatable.
open.criteria: Explain two distinct registers or modes, a transition and its possible impact.

C2.goal: Evaluate the speech’s argumentative tensions, identity work, rhetorical patterning and alternative interpretations.

gist.title: Which overarching tension is most central to the speech?
options: A public rejection of recognition conflicts with the speaker’s desire to win the prize.
A completed public achievement stands beside an unfinished personal ambition.
Artistic success is presented as the opposite of commitment to family life.
gist.why: He accepts a finished public accolade while describing an ongoing personal pursuit.

gist.title: What is the strongest explanation for the speech’s final tonal shift?
options: It blends public ceremony with an informal and recognisable persona.
It abandons the earlier personal themes for unrelated comic material.
It replaces direct address with a strictly institutional register.
gist.why: The close combines a serious occasion with conversational familiarity.

detail.title: Which inference about the opening acknowledgements is best supported?
options: They imply that collective credit makes individual honours logically invalid.
They serve chiefly to distance the speaker from the other nominees.
They frame the achievement generously without undermining its significance.
detail.why: He honours other performers while accepting his own recognition.

detail.title: What is the force of the transition from self-respect to respect for others?
options: It presents self-interest as incompatible with interpersonal obligations.
It implies that respecting others is unnecessary once one has self-esteem.
It reframes an apparently inward-looking value as a social one.
detail.why: The personal lesson is extended to an interpersonal ethic.

detail.title: What is the rhetorical effect of revisiting the opening framework in the closing moments?
options: It invalidates the original framework through contradictory examples.
It leaves the audience with a deliberately unresolved list of facts.
It produces coherence while expanding the focus to include listeners.
detail.why: The conclusion reconnects his strands and addresses the audience more widely.

sequence: He acknowledges other figures connected with the film.
He presents a brief organising device.
He turns to his late father.
He articulates a lesson from his upbringing.

facts.title: Give BOTH ages at which the speaker is questioned in the remembered conversations.

open.title: How does the ending of the speech relate to its opening? Argue your case.
open.answer: The close returns to the three-part framework; the Oscar marks an achievement while the hero story keeps the pursuit open, so the speech ends in productive tension rather than closure.
open.criteria: A clear thesis on how the ending relates to the opening, supported by two moments.
